experiments_or_tasks: Apply post-processing hard thresholding to reduce false discoveries and enforce exact acyclicity.
Develop an equality-constrained program for simultaneously estimating structure and parameters of a sparse DAG from possibly high-dimensional data.
Formulate DAG learning as a continuous optimization problem with a smooth equality constraint h(W)=0 that exactly characterizes acyclicity.
Solve the resulting program using standard numerical solvers (augmented Lagrangian with L-BFGS for smooth case, proximal quasi-Newton for L1-regularized case).

methods.name: NOTEARS
methods.protocol_description: The proposed method reformulates score-based DAG learning as a continuous optimization problem: min_W F(W) subject to h(W)=0, where h(W)=tr(e^{W∘W})-d is a smooth function that is zero iff W corresponds to a DAG. The problem is solved via the augmented Lagrangian method, converting it into a sequence of unconstrained subproblems. For λ=0 (no L1 penalty), L-BFGS is used; for λ>0, proximal quasi-Newton (PQN) is used. After obtaining a stationary point, hard thresholding with a fixed threshold ω is applied to remove small edges and ensure acyclicity.
